reserve_path.claim: New-block path: marks the sliver entry in the previous block by ANDing its u16 header with 0x3f (zeroes len, keeps wide/probe bits), then CurrentBlock++ (u32 at pool+8), CurrentByteOffset=0 (u32 at pool+0xC); if Blocks[CurrentBlock]==null it calls the same allocator: Malloc(0x20000, 2) and stores at [pool + CurrentBlock*8 + 0x10].

reserve_path.claim: Fit path does NOT touch CurrentBlock: CurrentBlock stays 0 until the first block boundary is crossed. Therefore a freshly initialized pool (or an early-game pool whose names still fit in block 0) legitimately has CurrentBlock == 0.

validator_predicates_recommended: Anchor: pool base file 0x9365ec0 / runtime 0x9765ec0; do NOT move it. The '0x9369ec0 correct-base' artifact was a tool offset bug and is retracted.

Blocks[0] (pool+0x10): must be nonzero once the bInitialized flag byte (pool-0x20, runtime 0x9765ea0) is 1. Its allocation is FMemory::Malloc(0x20000, align 2) from GMalloc: expect OS-heap-backed memory, >= 8-aligned (binned granularity is 16, so >=16-aligned in practice).

Do NOT require Blocks[0] to be outside the module image. Static evidence says OS-backed; the launch-9 observation pointed into the module BSS page range [0x970c000,0x9a34000) which overlaps LOAD7's memsz-only region - see UNRESOLVED. A 'readable + Blocks[0][0] header sane' predicate is safer than a region-class predicate.

CurrentBlock (u32 pool+8) semantics: index of the block currently being filled, 0-based; 0 is VALID after init (all early names live in block 0). Replace 'current_block >= 1' with 'id.block <= CurrentBlock' (exactly the engine getter TRUE 0x23d570 predicate).

CurrentByteOffset (u32 pool+0xC): must be < 0x20000; entry bounds check needed_bytes vs CurrentByteOffset only applies to the CURRENT block (id.block == CurrentBlock); completed blocks are full up to 0x20000 with a sliver-terminator header (& 0x3f) at their tail.

Entry identity check (cheap, strong): entry 0 of block 0 is 'None' stored by Init: u16 header at Blocks[0]+0 must satisfy hdr>>6 == 4 and (hdr&1) == 0 (ANSI), payload bytes +2..+6 == 'None'. This anchors base + Blocks[0] + stride-2 in one read.
id decomposition: block = id>>16, offset_units = id & 0xFFFF, byte offset = offset_units*2 (both engine ToString and Reserve agree).

NoneId/BytePropertyId at pool+0x14040/+0x14044 are real (init-verified strings); usable as secondary anchors, but note they live past the 256-bucket hash table at +0x10040 and the 256 aux entries ending at +0x1404C.
unresolved: launch-9 runtime observation 'Blocks[0] in ~[0x970c000,0x9a34000)' sits INSIDE LOAD7's memsz-only (BSS) runtime range [runtime 0x97085f2 .. 0x9a33418). Static analysis says Blocks[0] comes from the binned GMalloc (OS-backed). Possible explanations: (a) the launcher's region classifier merged the module BSS mapping with an adjacent heap mapping into one 'heap-class' span; (b) PS5 kernel places a heap arena overlapping what our file-based BSS math predicts (e.g. if runtime base differs from +0x400000 at that moment); (c) the observation itself was approximate ('~'). Could not be decided statically; needs a fresh runtime sample of the actual qword at 0x9765ed0 with the region map.

Exact PS5 page source under the binned slow path (TRUE 0x4b1460) was not traced to individual sce syscalls (recursive disasm of that region was misaligned; boundary detection there is harder due to dense code). No static-arena path was found, but 'OS pages' is inferred from the Binned2-family shape, not proven line-by-line.

Whether the thread-safety wrapper (vtable 0x7ec4030) is actually installed at runtime depends on the inner allocator's vtable+0xC0 return - statically undecidable; either way Malloc semantics are forwarding.
Role of the 256 aux sub-buffers (0x400 bytes each) at pool+0x1004C..0x1404C was not chased (not needed for Blocks[0] question).
Ghidra 12.1.4 headless analysis (194MB) was still running at delivery time; all claims above are Tier-1 capstone/lief evidence. Corroboration pass was not performed.
